full_judgment:
4. In support of the Rule, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the judgment of the lower appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as it did not advert to the reasonings of the trial Court and did not at all discuss the evidence on record for its own findings. The learned advocate for the petitioners submits that the trial Court on consideration of evidence on record found that there was no payment of earnest money but this finding was not at all reversed by the lower appellate Court although it discussed the evidence of P.W. l, P.W.6 and some averments made in the plaint in this respect. He next submitted that the lower appellate Court also did not discuss the evidence on record for its finding as to possession in the land. 

 8. Thus from reading of the judgment of the trial Court it appears that its findings were based on a thorough and detailed discussion of evidence on record. But the finding of the lower appellate court in reversing the findings of the trial court were based on surmises, conjectures and assumptions on record and without adverting to the reasons of the trial Court given for its findings. The lower appellate Court which is the last court of fact cannot arrive at the findings in the manner in which it has done in the instant case. In a case of affirmation, expression of general agreement by the lower Appellate Court with the reasons given by the trial court may be accepted as a good one and the confirming judgment need not go into every piece of evidence in great detail and adduce every reason for its conclusions. This view of mine finds support in the cases of Nagam Siva Reddy Vs. B Nazemuddin Saheb reported in 1966 A.P. 373 and in the case of Grija Nandini Devi & ors. Vs. Bijendra Narayan Chowdhury reported in 1967 SC 1124. But while reversing the finding of the trial court it is incumbent upon the lower appellate court to discuss the evidences led by the parties on the points upon which the findings of the trial court were given and to advert to the reasonings of the trial court for such findings. In this case I do not find from reading of the judgment of the lower appellate court that 'its judgment is in conformity with the aforesaid principles. In this view of the matter I hold that the judgment of lower Appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal. The lower Appellate Court should arrive at clear and definite findings on the points of prior talk regarding sale of the disputed land before the execution of kabalas, passing of consideration money for the kabalas, possession of the donees in the disputed land and of redemption of the mortgaged land on detailed discussion and consideration of evidences on record on each point.
